brief: Write the rules file for your system. Every rule must say how it is verified, by an automated check or by a named person.
do: Write at least six rules as RULE-1 to RULE-6 or more, each with a statement and a reason, covering structure, tools, data and approval.
Give every rule a VERIFIED_BY line naming the check, or a REVIEWED_BY line naming the role.
Add an owner, a date and a status (active, superseded or proposed) to the rules file.
Write the entry file of under 40 lines that points an agent to the rules, the decisions and the commands to build and test.
done: Rule quality: Specific statement and reason for every rule
Checks: Every rule has VERIFIED_BY or REVIEWED_BY
Currency: Owner, date and status on the file
Entry file: Short, with build and test commands and links to the detail
Evidence: The rules file with six or more rules, each with a check or a reviewer, and the entry file.
experienced: Apply it to an agent system you run or plan to run, with real tools, real limits, real owners and real dates.

hints.nudge: Specific statement and reason for every rule
Every rule has VERIFIED_BY or REVIEWED_BY
Owner, date and status on the file
Short, with build and test commands and links to the detail

mistakes: Checks: Some rules name a check
tips: Set a timer for the step and write a rough first version before you polish. A rough answer is easier to improve than a blank page.
Write for the next person who has to act on this, not for a marker. Use plain words and name things.
Stuck on your own system? Use the sample case in the worked example for this step, then come back to yours.
Prefer numbers, names and dates to adjectives. If you do not know a number, write your best estimate and label it as an estimate.
Save often. Your work stays in this browser only, so download your file at the end of every session.
example:
**Rules file (owner: tech lead, 2026-11-27, status: active)**

RULE-1: Only tools listed in the tool table may be called. Reason: unlisted tools have no contract. VERIFIED_BY: tests/policy/test_tool_allowlist.py
RULE-2: Order screens must not import the payment library; use PaymentPort. Reason: lets us swap providers. VERIFIED_BY: tests/architecture/test_imports.py
RULE-3: issue_refund accepts 1 to 100 TT$ and refuses a repeat refund. Reason: limits loss. VERIFIED_BY: tests/policy/test_refund_cap.py
RULE-4: Customer text is stored with source_label untrusted:customer. Reason: stops injected text acting as instruction. VERIFIED_BY: tests/data/test_labels.py
RULE-5: Refunds above TT$50 need vendor owner approval. Reason: money is hard to recall. VERIFIED_BY: tests/policy/test_approval.py
RULE-6: A new external service needs a decision record. Reason: keeps decisions visible. REVIEWED_BY: tech lead in pull request review

**Entry file (AGENTS.md).** What the system is; how to build and test; the six rules; where decisions live; what to do if unsure: stop and ask.
